- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After recent spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next period; cap forecast peak at +10% above prior high or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive (especially > 0.3), model frequently overestimates upward momentum; reduce forecast slope or apply downward bias of 1–2% to prevent overbought bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast if recent 7-day average is below 68.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often lags true trend by 1–2 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward tilt if sentiment is trending up.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment is explicitly bullish (>0.3) and recent price is >70; use 3-day moving average to filter noise before forecasting.
